title: dispatcher: 'gh --jq --arg' is malformed; both follow-up and conflict dispatchers silently fail every cycle
description:
## Problem

**Severity: high** — silent correctness bug in both `loop_dispatcher_followup` and `loop_dispatcher_conflicts`. They've been completely non-functional whenever the loop runs against a real GitHub repo: the follow-up dispatcher never invokes `run-developer.sh follow-up <PR>` after a reviewer-agent verdict, and the conflict dispatcher never invokes `resolve-conflicts <PR>` for CONFLICTING PRs. The reviewer agent itself works (its eligibility doesn't use `gh --jq --arg`), so the loop appears healthy — verdicts get posted — but every downstream effect is dead.

## Repro

Hit while debugging why nothing followed-up on aniryou/youtube-clipper#4 after the reviewer posted `[reviewer-agent: comment]`. Dispatcher pane logs:

  [dispatch:followup] scanning open dev-agent PRs...
  [dispatch:followup] sleeping 60s...

— nothing in between. Direct reproduction:

  $ gh pr list --repo aniryou/youtube-clipper --state open \
      --json number,headRefName,isDraft \
      --jq --arg prefix "dev-agent/" \
          '.[] | select(.headRefName | startswith(\$prefix)) | ... | .number'
  unknown arguments ["prefix" "dev-agent/" ".[] | ..."]; please quote all values that have spaces
  exit=1

## Root cause — where the bug lives

- `runners/run-loop.sh:183-188` — follow-up dispatcher's `gh pr list`.
- `runners/run-loop.sh:224-232` — conflict dispatcher's `gh pr list`.

Both pass `--jq --arg prefix "${BRANCH_PREFIX}/"`. `gh`'s `--jq` is a single-string flag; it consumes the literal `--arg` as its value, leaving `prefix`, `dev-agent/`, and the actual jq expression as unrecognized positional args. The error is suppressed via `2>/dev/null`, so the failure is invisible at the pane level. `while IFS= read -r pr` reads zero PRs and the loop body never executes.

## Proposed fix

Inline the prefix into the jq expression via shell interpolation. `gh --jq` accepts a regular jq filter — drop the attempt to use jq's own `--arg`:

  gh pr list --repo "\$REPO_SLUG" --state open \\
    --json number,headRefName,isDraft \\
    --jq ".[] | select(.headRefName | startswith(\\\"\${BRANCH_PREFIX}/\\\")) | select(.isDraft == false) | .number" \\
    2>/dev/null

Same shape for the conflict dispatcher (with the extra `mergeable == "CONFLICTING"` clause). Two locations.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring the `2>/dev/null` swallowing pattern more broadly. Worth a separate issue — a stderr-to-pane handler would have made this self-evident from minute one.
- Changing dispatcher gating logic (the `latest_review > latest_devcomment` comparison itself is correct).

## References

- `runners/run-loop.sh:183-188`, `runners/run-loop.sh:224-232`
- `aniryou/youtube-clipper#4` — PR where this was discovered
acceptance_criteria:
- Both `gh pr list` invocations exit 0 and emit one PR number per line for matching PRs.
- After the fix, on a repo with a reviewed dev-agent PR awaiting follow-up: `[dispatch:followup] dispatching follow-up for PR #N (review=... dev=none)` appears in the pane within one POLL_INTERVAL of `st loop start`.
- All existing tests still pass (`bats tests/`).
- New `tests/test_dispatchers.bats` covers the jq filter against fixture PR lists, mirroring the `tests/test_eligibility.bats:47-78` pattern.

title: dev workers thunder: introduce random startup jitter so parallel instances don't compete for the same issues
description:
## Problem

When `st loop start --dev-instances=N` (N > 1) creates multiple dev-agent panes, all N workers enter `loop_dev_mode1` at near-identical timestamps. They all then:

1. Call `eligibility_dev_count` against the same gh state, see the same eligible issues.
2. Race to `mkdir $LOCK_DIR/gh-<n>.lock` — exactly one wins per issue, N-1 lose.
3. Losers exit after a wasted scan; winners proceed.

The existing lock-dir filter in `runners/lib/eligibility.sh:47-71` mitigates this *after the first cycle* (a worker that lost the race sees the lock present on its next scan), but the **simultaneous startup window** still produces N-1 wasted invocations on the very first cycle. Same problem recurs after any empty cycle: all workers sleep `POLL_INTERVAL` and wake simultaneously.

The eligibility-predicate file already calls out this exact cost path:

  > Without [the lock-dir post-filter], every parallel wrapper sees the same gh
  > count, every wrapper invokes the LLM, and N-1 lose the lock race and exit
  > after a wasted scan — the dominant cost path under DEV_INSTANCES>1.

The lock-dir filter is a partial fix; jitter is the complementary fix.

## Current behavior — where the gap lives

- `runners/run-loop.sh:91-113` — `loop_dev_mode1` enters its `while true` loop immediately, no startup delay. Sleep duration is deterministic (`POLL_INTERVAL` or `empty_cycle_sleep`).
- `runners/run-loop.sh:386-396` — `tmux send-keys` fires the loop command into each dev pane sequentially but in tight succession. Effective startup skew between panes is well under one POLL_INTERVAL.

## Proposed fix

Add a per-instance random jitter at the top of `loop_dev_mode1`, before the `while true`. Range `0..POLL_INTERVAL` seconds gives each worker a unique phase offset that persists across cycles (since they all sleep the same fixed POLL_INTERVAL after that). One-time cost; trivial.

  loop_dev_mode1() {
    local id="\$1"
    local empty_streak=0 ec sleep_for jitter
    jitter=\$(( (RANDOM % POLL_INTERVAL) + 1 ))
    echo "[\$(ts)] [dev-\${id}] startup jitter: sleeping \${jitter}s before first cycle"
    sleep "\$jitter"
    while true; do
      ...

Optionally extend to the reviewer + dispatchers (same pattern), but they're single-instance so the win is small.

## Out of scope

- Adding per-cycle jitter on top of the fixed `POLL_INTERVAL` sleep. Worth considering if startup jitter doesn't fully de-converge the workers in practice (LLM-call durations vary, so they should drift naturally), but not needed for v1.
- Jittering the reviewer / dispatcher panes — single-instance, so nothing to thunder against.
- Tuning POLL_INTERVAL or the empty-cycle backoff curve.

## References

- `runners/run-loop.sh:91-113` — `loop_dev_mode1`, no jitter
- `runners/lib/eligibility.sh:34-46` — comment acknowledging the wasted-scan cost path under DEV_INSTANCES>1
- `runners/run-loop.sh:386-396` — tmux send-keys (where simultaneity originates)
acceptance_criteria:
- `loop_dev_mode1` sleeps a per-instance random duration in `[1, POLL_INTERVAL]` seconds before its first cycle.
- Jitter is logged: `[dev-<id>] startup jitter: sleeping <N>s before first cycle`.
- With `DEV_INSTANCES=3` and a single eligible issue, exactly one worker claims the lock and runs the LLM; the other two see the lock present in their (delayed) eligibility scan and exit early without invoking `claude`. Verifiable via /tmp logs.
- `tests/test_loop_jitter.bats` (new): exercises the jitter range — invoking the function 50× with `RANDOM` controlled, the produced sleep values cover at least 80% of the `[1..POLL_INTERVAL]` range and never exceed POLL_INTERVAL.
- All existing tests still pass (`bats tests/`).

title: eligibility_review_pending: 'commit_id' is always null in 'gh pr view --json reviews'; predicate over-reports
description:
## Problem

**Severity: medium** — `eligibility_review_pending` filters reviews by `.commit_id` to determine whether a `[reviewer-agent: ...]` review is at the PR's current head. But `gh pr view --json reviews` (and `gh pr list --json reviews`) populates `commit_id` as `null` regardless of the actual commit. So the `index($pr.headRefOid)` lookup never matches, every reviewed PR is always counted as "needs review", and the reviewer agent fires on every poll cycle only to skip itself via the orchestrator's separate idempotence check.

Wasteful (LLM cost ~$0.12/run × every POLL_INTERVAL) but not silently incorrect — the orchestrator's idempotence check catches the over-fire. Why severity:medium rather than high: the orchestrator catches it; only the LLM cost is the impact.

## Repro

aniryou/youtube-clipper#4 has had ~10 reviewer-agent log files in /tmp over a 20-min span, each ending with "PR is already reviewed at the current head SHA" and skipping. Direct verification:

  $ gh pr view 4 --repo aniryou/youtube-clipper --json reviews \\
      | jq '.reviews[0].commit_id'
  null

## Root cause — where the bug lives

- `runners/lib/eligibility.sh:88-100` — uses `map(select(.body | test(\$re)) | .commit_id) | index(\$pr.headRefOid) | not`.
- `tests/fixtures/gh/prs-current.json`, `prs-stale.json`, `prs-mixed.json` — fixtures hand-include `commit_id` per review, so `tests/test_eligibility.bats:53-78` passes. Fixture-vs-reality drift.

## Proposed fix

Compare review `submittedAt` against the PR head commit's `committedDate`: treat any `[reviewer-agent: ...]` review submitted after the head's `committedDate` as covering it. `committedDate` is available via `gh pr view --json commits` (last entry). No new dependency, matches the follow-up dispatcher's `submittedAt`-based style.

Alternative: switch to GraphQL `reviews(last: N) { commit { oid } }`. Heavier, not needed.

## Out of scope

- The reviewer orchestrator's own idempotence check (the orchestrator does its own `gh pr view` and matches `[reviewer-agent: ...]` differently — that path is correct).
- Adding a generic GraphQL-based predicate.

## References

- `runners/lib/eligibility.sh:88-100`
- `tests/test_eligibility.bats:47-78` — tests passing against drifted fixtures
- `aniryou/youtube-clipper#4` — repro PR
- Related: the dispatcher `gh --jq --arg` bug (loop-3s7, severity:high)
acceptance_criteria:
- `eligibility_review_pending` returns 0 for PRs whose latest `[reviewer-agent: ...]` review's `submittedAt` is later than the head commit's `committedDate`.
- Returns 1 for PRs with no agent review.
- Returns 1 for PRs with a stale review (review `submittedAt` predates current head `committedDate`).
- Existing fixtures (`prs-current.json`, `prs-stale.json`, `prs-mixed.json`) are updated to drop `commit_id` and add `commits` + per-review `submittedAt` so fixtures match real `gh` output.

title: eligibility_dev_count: replace search-index query with REST list endpoint
description:
## Problem

`eligibility_dev_count` in `runners/lib/eligibility.sh:47-66` queries the GitHub **search index** via `gh issue list --search "label:..." no:assignee`. The search endpoint is silently lossy in two ways that have been hit in practice:

1. **Index lag** on freshly-created issues — minutes to hours before they're searchable, even though they're returned by the REST list endpoint immediately.
2. **GitHub's automated content filter** silently hides certain issues from the search index entirely (e.g. duplicate titles, code-dense bodies on new repos). Affected issues remain visible via the REST list endpoint and via GraphQL.

When either condition hits, the dev-agent reports `eligibility: no eligible issues` and parks at the 300s backoff cap, even though `gh issue view` and the GitHub UI's direct link both show the issue is open and labeled correctly.

## Repro

Hit today on `aniryou/youtube-clipper#1` and `#3` (identical titles + code-dense bodies). Both issues were `OPEN`, had `severity:medium` + `enhancement`, no assignee. The eligibility predicate returned 0 candidates; `gh issue list` (no `--search`) returned both.

```
# returns []
gh issue list --repo aniryou/youtube-clipper --state open \
  --search 'label:"severity:high","severity:medium" no:assignee' --json number

# returns all 3 issues
gh issue list --repo aniryou/youtube-clipper --state open --json number
```

## Proposed fix

Switch `eligibility_dev_count` from the search endpoint to the REST list endpoint. List supports `--label` filtering directly and `assignees` via the JSON projection, so we can replicate the same predicate without the search-index dependency.

Sketch:

```bash
nums_high=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO_SLUG" --state open \
  --label "$SEVERITY_LABEL_HIGH" --json number,assignees --limit 50 \
  | jq -r '.[] | select(.assignees == []) | .number')
nums_med=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO_SLUG" --state open \
  --label "$SEVERITY_LABEL_MEDIUM" --json number,assignees --limit 50 \
  | jq -r '.[] | select(.assignees == []) | .number')
nums=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$nums_high" "$nums_med" | sort -u | grep . || true)
```

Two `gh` calls instead of one, but each is cheap and the cost dominates the search call anyway. Same lock-dir post-filter as today.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bash runners/lib/eligibility.sh dev` returns the correct count for issues that the REST list endpoint can see, regardless of search-index state.
- Re-running the predicate on the `aniryou/youtube-clipper` repo (which currently has the filter actively hiding `#3`) returns ≥1 candidate immediately, with no waiting on the search index.
- `eligibility_review_pending` is unaffected (it queries PRs, not issues, and uses a `head:` qualifier where search is appropriate).

## Out of scope

- Re-architecting the dev-agent's atomic-claim path (still uses `mkdir` lock under `LOCK_DIR`).
- Adding GraphQL-based predicates as a generic alternative.
- Anything to do with the GitHub UI filter itself — that's GitHub's behavior to live with.

## References

- `runners/lib/eligibility.sh:47-66` — current implementation
- `runners/run-developer.sh:64-77` — wrapper that consumes the exit code
- `aniryou/youtube-clipper#1`, `#3` — the issues that triggered discovery
close_reason: Fixed in commit 14d5a05 — switched to REST list endpoint with per-label calls and client-side assignee filter; added 3 bats tests.

title: add 'st onboard' to audit a repo for loop's prerequisites
description:
The loop framework assumes scaffolding it doesn't currently verify: pre-commit hooks (so dev-agent commits get auto-formatted before push), GitHub Actions CI (so the agent has a real signal to gate merge on — without it, 'gh pr checks' returns vacuously-green and the agent ships junk), a test runner with at least one test (so CI's signal is meaningful and the agent's CI-retry loop has something to read from on red), and a canonical GitHub label set (so the eligibility predicate's `--label severity:high|medium` queries match real labels and the issue-author agent has consistent labels to apply).

Today, a user retrofitting loop onto an existing repo finds out about each missing piece by reading prompt failures or by debugging a silent merge of broken code. For labels specifically, missing-label issues manifest as `eligibility_dev_count` always returning 0 and the dev-agent parking — the same symptom as the search-index bug just fixed in loop-d8j, but with a different root cause. 'st onboard' should walk the repo once, report pass/fail per check, and emit copy-pasteable fix snippets for each gap so the user can either fix manually or pipe through bash.
design:
New file: bin/st gains 'onboard' subcommand → calls lib/onboard.sh.

New file: templates/labels.json — canonical loop label set, source of truth for both the audit predicate and the auto-create writer. JSON over YAML to avoid a yq dependency (jq is already required). Schema:
  [
    {"name": "severity:high",   "color": "d73a4a", "description": "Silent correctness bug, security issue, or blocker"},
    {"name": "severity:medium", "color": "fbca04", "description": "Noticeable defect or missing feature with clear current use case"},
    {"name": "severity:low",    "color": "0e8a16", "description": "Nice-to-have, polish, or unlikely edge case"},
    {"name": "bug",             "color": "d73a4a", "description": "Existing functionality is broken"},
    {"name": "enhancement",     "color": "a2eeef", "description": "New functionality or extension of existing"},
    {"name": "testing",         "color": "bfdadc", "description": "Tests, test infrastructure, or CI test wiring"},
    {"name": "documentation",   "color": "0075ca", "description": "Docs/comments only, no behavior change"}
  ]

lib/onboard.sh structure:
  - Each check is a named function returning 0/1 + an OK/FAIL printout
  - Functions: check_loop_config, check_beads, check_gh_auth, check_labels, check_pre_commit_config, check_pre_commit_installed, check_ci_workflow, check_ci_pr_trigger, check_test_dir, check_test_files, check_worktree_base
  - Aggregator runs them all, accumulates pass/fail tally, prints fix snippets for fails
  - Fix snippets live inline in each check function — kept close to the predicate so they don't drift

check_labels behavior (the one exception to the read-only stance):
  - Read templates/labels.json, query 'gh label list --repo $REPO_SLUG --json name', diff
  - On FAIL: auto-create missing labels via 'gh label create' (idempotent — skip-if-exists semantics)
  - Prints one '+ created <name>' line per label written
  - Existing labels are NOT modified (color/description drift reported but not corrected in v1)
  - Rationale for the exception: label creation is mechanical, idempotent, and non-destructive. Read-only stance is preserved for every other check (pre-commit, CI workflow, test files, etc.) where mutating the repo carries real risk.

Output format:
  ✓ loop.config           REPO_SLUG=aniryou/foo
  ✓ .beads/
  ✓ gh auth (aniryou)
  ✓ labels (auto-created severity:high, severity:medium, testing)
  ✗ .pre-commit-config.yaml
      Fix: cat > .pre-commit-config.yaml <<'EOF2'
           repos:
             - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
               rev: v0.7.4
               ...
           EOF2
           pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install
  ✗ CI workflow
      Fix: mkdir -p .github/workflows
           cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml <<'EOF2' ...
  ...

  Result: 8/11 checks passed; 3 missing. Run 'st onboard -v' for details.

Out of scope (file separately):
  - 'st onboard --fix' to auto-apply fixes for the *other* checks (still risky; v1 leaves those writes to the user)
  - Updating colors/descriptions of existing labels (drift correction). v1 only creates missing labels; correcting drift is a follow-up
  - Language-specific test scaffolding (Python pytest vs Node jest etc.) — onboard reports presence; doesn't generate
  - Per-repo override of which checks apply (e.g. 'this repo doesn't need GH Actions because it uses CircleCI')
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st onboard' runs from anywhere inside a repo (walks up to find .loop/loop.config) and prints a pass/fail report
- Read-only by default for every check EXCEPT check_labels — never mutates the repo or runs install commands without explicit '--fix' (out of scope for v1)
- check_labels auto-creates any missing canonical labels via 'gh label create' (idempotent). Prints one '+ created <name>' line per label written. Existing labels are NOT modified (color/description drift reported but not corrected in v1).
- Exit code 0 if all checks pass, 1 if any fail (suitable for CI-style usage)
- Each failed check prints a concrete copy-pasteable fix command/snippet (except check_labels, which fixes itself)
- Checks performed (in order):
  • .loop/loop.config exists AND REPO_OWNER/REPO_NAME are not the example placeholders
  • .beads/ exists (bd is the canonical task tracker per CLAUDE.md)
  • gh CLI authenticated for REPO_SLUG (gh auth status -h github.com)
  • canonical labels exist on $REPO_SLUG per templates/labels.json; missing ones are auto-created
  • .pre-commit-config.yaml exists at repo root
  • pre-commit hooks actually installed (.git/hooks/pre-commit has the pre-commit-installed marker)
  • .github/workflows/ has at least one .yml/.yaml file
  • The first workflow runs on pull_request events (grep 'on:' block)
  • A test directory exists (tests/ or test/ at repo root)
  • At least one test file exists in that directory (test_*.py / *_test.py / *.test.{js,ts} / *_test.go)
  • WORKTREE_BASE is writable (try mkdir -p; rmdir)
- Verbose mode '-v' shows what each check tested and which path it inspected

title: add 'st permissions install' to bootstrap user-level Claude grants
description: When a new user installs loop, Claude Code re-prompts them for every Bash/MCP grant the agents need (gh, git, bd, python, pre-commit, tmux, …). A self-contained 'st permissions install' command should remove that friction so onboarding a repo is genuinely one-step.
design:
Subcommand 'permissions' added to bin/st with dispatch to lib/permissions.sh.

Grant list lives in lib/permissions.json — single source of truth, readable by users.
Scope = grants the four loop agents actually invoke; NOT personal QoL:
  gh *, git *, bd *, st *, python *, python3 *, pytest *,
  pre-commit run *, ruff *, tmux *, pkill *, kill *, bash, jq *, mkdir *, chmod *

Implementation:
  - lib/permissions.sh reads lib/permissions.json (jq parses)
  - Reads existing ~/.claude/settings.json (creates from template if missing)
  - Computes set difference (new - existing) using jq
  - On install: cp settings.json settings.json.loop.bak; jq merge writes new file
  - On --dry-run: print the diff list (one entry per line)
  - On list: cat lib/permissions.json | jq '.allow'
  - Atomic write: jq → temp file → mv into place

Out of scope (file separately if needed):
  - Project-specific grants (e.g. .venv/, PYTHONPATH=src) — those still belong in repo's .claude/settings.local.json
  - 'st permissions uninstall' (revert to backup) — nice-to-have, not in v1
  - Auto-running install during 'st init' — keep explicit; user opts in
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st permissions install' merges loop-required grants into ~/.claude/settings.json
- Idempotent: re-running adds nothing if all entries already present (compare by exact string match)
- '--dry-run' prints the diff (entries that would be added) and exits 0 without writing
- 'st permissions list' prints the grant list as JSON (no I/O on settings.json)
- A backup is written to ~/.claude/settings.json.loop.bak before any modification
- New ~/.claude/ is handled: creates settings.json with {permissions: {allow: [...]}} if missing
- JSON is validated (jq -e .) before and after; refuses to write if pre-state is invalid
- Clear error if jq is missing on PATH ('install jq via brew install jq')
- Top-level non-permission keys (e.g. effortLevel, skipAutoPermissionPrompt) are preserved

title: st init: write a LOOP marker-block into the repo's CLAUDE.md
description:
Loop currently has no programmatic way to communicate framework-specific guidance to a Claude session running inside a consumer repo. A human Claude session has no idea that the dev-agent owns 'BRANCH_PREFIX/*' branches, that locks live under LOCK_DIR, or which 'st *' commands are available — it has to be told manually each time, or the user has to hand-write the same boilerplate into every consumer repo's CLAUDE.md.

Mirror bd's pattern: a marker-bracketed block in CLAUDE.md, written by 'st init' and refreshed by a future 'st sync'. Closes the onboarding loop — 'st init' writes loop.config AND the CLAUDE.md block, so a new repo is genuinely one-step.
design:
New template: templates/claude-md-block.md — parameterized, rendered through the existing lib/render-prompt.sh pipeline.

bin/st cmd_init extended: after copying loop.config from the example, render claude-md-block.md and either:
  - append it to existing CLAUDE.md (between markers, preserving the rest), OR
  - write a new CLAUDE.md containing only the block + a stub heading

Hash computed by piping rendered block (without marker lines) into 'shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-8' and substituted into the BEGIN marker.

Idempotency: a small awk/sed pass detects the BEGIN/END pair. If present, skip; if absent, append. (Refresh-when-hash-stale is the 'st sync' job.)

Out of scope (file separately if/when needed):
  - 'st sync' to refresh the block on framework upgrade
  - Auto-detection of stale blocks across consumer repos
  - Per-repo customization of block content (beyond loop.config substitutions)
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st init' writes a LOOP marker-block into the repo's CLAUDE.md
- Creates CLAUDE.md if it doesn't exist; preserves all user content outside the block if it does
- Idempotent: re-running 'st init' does not duplicate the block; if a block exists, leaves it alone (refresh is the future 'st sync' job)
- Marker format mirrors bd: <!-- BEGIN LOOP INTEGRATION v:1 hash:<sha8> --> ... <!-- END LOOP INTEGRATION -->
- Block content includes:
  - one-paragraph mental model (this repo is a loop consumer; framework lives at ~/code/loop)
  - command reference (st dev / st review / st loop start / st help)
  - coordinate-with-dev-agent rules (don't push to BRANCH_PREFIX/*, don't tamper with LOCK_DIR, dev-agent uses filesystem locks for atomic claim)
  - pointer to .loop/loop.config for tunables
- Block is parameterized — loop.config variables (BRANCH_PREFIX, LOCK_DIR, etc.) substituted via the existing render-prompt.sh
- Block hash is sha256 of rendered content truncated to 8 chars (used by future 'st sync' for drift detection)
- AGENTS.md is NOT touched — bd's choice to write to both files is a redundancy we don't repeat

title: refresh stale CLAUDE.md marker-block when framework upgrades (st sync vs implicit)
description:
Once the LOOP marker-block ships and 'st init' writes a block with a content hash, consumer repos will go stale silently when ~/code/loop is git-pulled and the template changes. Need a way to detect and refresh stale blocks.

DESIGN QUESTION (deliberately deferred until the first real stale-block moment): explicit 'st sync' command vs implicit refresh on every 'st *' invocation (the pattern bd uses). bd's implicit approach is ergonomically nicer — no command to remember, never out of date — but adds a cost (and a moving target) to every CLI call. Decide based on (a) how often templates actually change, (b) whether there's ever a multi-repo propagation pain.

Filed P4: don't build until there's evidence of need (a template change worth propagating across multiple repos).
design:
Two paths to evaluate when this is built:

A) Explicit 'st sync':
   - bin/st adds 'sync' subcommand
   - lib/sync.sh: render template → hash → compare to repo's marker → if stale, replace block
   - User must remember to run after 'cd ~/code/loop && git pull'

B) Implicit refresh:
   - Wrap every 'st *' subcommand entry in a stale-block check
   - On stale: print one-line notice + refresh + continue
   - Cache last-seen-template-hash in ~/.cache/loop/ to keep the check cheap

Recommendation when building: start with B (matches bd's pattern; ergonomically cleaner) but only if multi-repo propagation is real. If single-repo is permanent, neither is worth building — just re-run 'st init --force-block-refresh' manually after big upgrades.

Out of scope:
  - Refreshing loop.config (different problem; user values must not be clobbered)
  - Cross-repo discovery (loop doesn't track which repos exist)
acceptance_criteria:
- Detect stale marker-block: compare hash in CLAUDE.md's BEGIN marker against fresh hash of rendered current template
- Refresh stale block in place, preserving all CLAUDE.md content outside the markers
- Picked design (explicit 'st sync' or implicit on every 'st *') is informed by actual usage, not guessed
- If implicit: refresh path adds no measurable latency to common commands (cache the hash check)
- If explicit: 'st sync' is idempotent (no-op when already current) and supports '--dry-run' to print the diff
